Cyber Security


Palo Alto Networks Firewall Zero-Day Exploited by State Actors for Nearly a Month


May 7, 24:00


Palo Alto Networks revealed that suspected state-sponsored hackers have been actively exploiting a critical PAN-OS firewall vulnerability (CVE-2026-0300) since April 9, 2026. The buffer overflow flaw in the User-ID Authentication Portal enables unauthenticated remote code execution with a CVSS score of 9.3. The vulnerability affects PA and VM series firewalls when the portal is internet-accessible, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code without authentication.


Critical network infrastructure vulnerability affecting enterprise firewalls globally, requiring immediate patching to prevent complete network compromise


Sources: BleepingComputer · Cybersecurity News


Claude AI Weaponized in Critical Infrastructure Attack on Mexican Water Utility


May 7, 24:00


Threat actors used Anthropic's Claude AI to identify and target operational technology assets during an intrusion at a water and drainage utility in Monterrey, Mexico in January 2026. The attack represents one of the first documented cases where adversaries leveraged commercial AI tools to enhance critical infrastructure attacks. The incident demonstrates how AI capabilities can be weaponized to improve reconnaissance and targeting of industrial control systems.


First documented case of AI being used to enhance attacks against critical infrastructure, potentially signaling a new evolution in nation-state and criminal attack capabilities


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Critical Ollama Memory Leak Exposes 300,000 AI Servers Globally


May 7, 24:00


A vulnerability dubbed 'Bleeding Llama' allows unauthenticated attackers to extract sensitive data directly from memory on Ollama servers running local AI models. The flaw affects approximately 300,000 internet-facing servers worldwide that use the popular platform for running local AI models. Successful exploitation enables attackers to access the Ollama process and steal sensitive information without authentication.


Major AI infrastructure vulnerability affecting hundreds of thousands of servers and demonstrating security risks in the rapidly growing local AI deployment ecosystem


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Critical vm2 Node.js Library Vulnerabilities Enable Sandbox Escapes


May 7, 24:00


Eleven critical vulnerabilities were discovered in the vm2 Node.js sandbox library, affecting all versions up to 3.11.1. Each flaw provides attackers with a clear path to escape the sandbox and execute arbitrary code on host systems. The vulnerabilities pose severe risks to applications using vm2 for running untrusted JavaScript code in secure environments.


Critical vulnerability in popular JavaScript security library affecting code isolation across numerous applications and potentially enabling widespread supply chain attacks


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Redis Critical Vulnerabilities Enable Remote Code Execution on Cloud and Enterprise Deployments


May 7, 24:00


Five dangerous vulnerabilities affect Redis Cloud, Redis Software, and open-source community editions, enabling authenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution. All flaws require authenticated access but successful exploitation can lead to arbitrary code execution, full system compromise, and data exfiltration. The vulnerabilities impact one of the most widely-used in-memory data structure stores across enterprise deployments.


Critical database infrastructure vulnerabilities affecting widely-deployed Redis systems across cloud and enterprise environments


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Fake Claude AI Website Distributes New Beagle Windows Backdoor


May 7, 24:00


A fraudulent Claude AI website is delivering a previously undocumented Windows backdoor called Beagle through fake Claude-Pro Relay downloads. The malicious site mimics the legitimate Claude interface to trick users into downloading and installing the backdoor malware. The campaign demonstrates how threat actors are leveraging AI tool popularity to distribute malware through convincing fake websites.

Users are discovering unexplained drops in available storage as Chrome installs this large on-device AI model in browser directories.

Brussels describes the delay as simplification efforts, though critics view it as a retreat from regulatory enforcement. The postponement affects timeline for AI system compliance requirements across the bloc.
